name: Vesperite-NR
description: A metamaterial alloy structured at the quantum level to possess a negative refractive index across visible and near-infrared spectra, bending incident light smoothly around any object clad in it rather than reflecting or absorbing. Vesperite-NR is not a coating but a structural metal — it can be formed into load-bearing panels, armor plates, and chassis components while maintaining its photonic properties. Fabricated by Apex Nanofabrication using resonant plasma deposition of silver-gallium-niobium lattices tuned to sub-wavelength periodicity.
cost: Φ 380,000 per kg — restricted, military contract only
story_hooks: A Vesperite-NR panel has surfaced in a Shelf-tier black market, cut into small squares and sold as 'ghost tiles' — someone raided a military shipment, and both the military and the thieves are moving through the lower tiers looking for it.

A Spire architect incorporated Vesperite-NR into a private residence as an aesthetic feature — the owner has since disappeared, and the house appears empty from every sensor and visual angle, making investigation nearly impossible.

Apex Nanofabrication's lead resonance engineer claims the negative-index lattice occasionally exhibits anomalous behavior — objects cloaked for extended periods seem to develop minor quantum decoherence effects in nearby organic tissue.
